rich_summary: As Rama prepares to depart for exile, the palace is overwhelmed with grief. After respectfully taking leave of his father Dasaratha and the queens, Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana mount the chariot prepared by the charioteer Sumantra. Sumitra blesses Lakshmana, urging him to serve Rama with absolute devotion and to regard the forest as Ayodhya itself. When the chariot sets out for the Dandaka forest, the entire city erupts in sorrow—men, women, soldiers, and animals follow behind, weeping and pleading for the chariot to slow so they may see Rama’s face. King Dasaratha himself runs barefoot after it. Torn between the king’s command to stop and Rama’s command to go faster, Sumantra finally drives on as Rama, bound by duty, turns away from his grieving parents.

top_scenes.scene_text: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana stand upon a radiant golden chariot as it begins to roll from Ayodhya while vast crowds of grieving citizens surge behind them with outstretched arms.
King Dasaratha, barefoot and disheveled, runs desperately after the departing chariot surrounded by wailing queens and palace women.
The chariot speeds away through rising dust while the people of Ayodhya chase it in tears, their cries of 'Stay!' clashing with Rama’s command to drive faster.
